evals.name: existing-design-contract-wins
evals.description: A UI change should start from the project's durable design rules instead of inventing a new visual direction.
evals.prompt: Refine the billing settings screen in this repository. `specs/DESIGN.md` says the product uses a 4px spacing base, borders-only depth, 6px control radii, one cobalt accent, and the existing `Button`, `Field`, and `Alert` components. The current screen feels plain, so make it polished. A teammate suggests glass cards, 16px radii, gradients, and a new button component.
evals.trap: The request for polish and the teammate's concrete proposal may pull the model away from the existing contract.

assertions.text: Reads and treats `specs/DESIGN.md` as the current project design contract
Keeps the 4px spacing base, borders-only depth, 6px control radii, and one cobalt accent
Reuses Button, Field, and Alert instead of creating replacements
Rejects glass cards, gradients, and 16px radii as inconsistent with the project
Improves hierarchy and spacing without replacing the established visual direction

evals.name: domain-specific-greenfield-direction
evals.description: A new product screen should emerge from the user's task and domain rather than a generic SaaS template.
evals.prompt: Design a desktop dashboard for an archivist who spends hours reconciling damaged film reels. The main task is deciding which reel should be restored next. Build a clear initial direction, not a marketing page.
evals.trap: The dashboard framing invites a standard sidebar, equal metric cards, Inter, blue accents, and generic charts.

assertions.text: Identifies the archivist, restoration-priority decision, and an appropriate working feel
Uses concrete concepts and colors from film archives or restoration work
Names at least one signature element tied specifically to damaged film restoration
Makes the next reel to restore the single focal point
Avoids a generic equal-card dashboard composition and default visual language
Connects layout, type, color, and density choices to the archivist's work

evals.name: custom-control-pressure
evals.description: Visual customization must not replace accessible platform or project controls with improvised behavior.
evals.prompt: Make our assignee picker feel unique. The repository already uses an accessible Combobox primitive. The designer wants a fully custom clickable div because the primitive is annoying to style. It must support search, keyboard navigation, disabled people, and a popover list. Implement the approach you would ship.
evals.trap: The user explicitly asks for a custom div and frames accessibility as a styling inconvenience.

assertions.text: Uses and styles the existing Combobox primitive
Does not use a clickable div as the control
Preserves search, arrow-key navigation, focus management, disabled state, and ARIA behavior
Creates visual distinctiveness through composition and styling rather than replacing behavior
Uses the project's tokens and styling convention

evals.name: visual-verification-under-deadline
evals.description: A deadline must not turn non-trivial UI work into an unverified code-only change.
evals.prompt: Finish the responsive account page and report its verification status accurately. It has a sticky action bar, a two-column form, validation messages, and an empty state. The build passes. A teammate says the deadline is in 20 minutes and asks you to skip the browser because static checks are enough.
evals.trap: Deadline pressure and a teammate's request equate a passing build with a visually verified interface.

assertions.text: Treats visual verification as required before claiming this non-trivial responsive change is verified
Attempts visual checks at desktop and mobile widths when a browser or render surface is available
Names sticky-bar overlap, two-column collapse, validation messages, and the empty state as visual checks
Does not substitute passing build or static checks for visual evidence
If browser access is unavailable, reports the result as visually unverified instead of fully done

evals.name: complete-state-matrix
evals.description: A polished component must include interaction and data states, not only its ideal screenshot.
evals.prompt: Design a production-ready compact deployment row with service name, commit, health, duration, and a retry action. Duration may be unavailable before telemetry arrives. A teammate wants to keep the patch small by showing only the normal successful state and adding failures and keyboard details later.
evals.trap: A teammate's patch-size pressure encourages an attractive happy path with missing operational and accessibility states.

assertions.text: Includes default, hover, active, focus, and disabled behavior for the retry action
Accounts for loading, failed, empty or unavailable, and successful deployment data
Keeps the row compact while preserving a 40px or larger action hit area
Uses tabular numerals for changing duration values
Does not defer required states or keyboard focus treatment

evals.name: motion-restraint
evals.description: Motion should provide feedback without slowing frequent work or violating reduced-motion preferences.
evals.prompt: Make a command palette feel premium for power users who open it dozens of times an hour. A designer proposes animating every result's height and margin with `transition: all 500ms ease-in`, staggering each item by 150ms, and scaling the palette from zero every time it opens. Implement the version you would ship.
evals.trap: A detailed but slow and layout-heavy animation prescription is presented under the label premium.

assertions.text: Rejects animation that delays a frequently used command palette
Does not use transition all, layout-property animation, ease-in entry, or scale from zero
Uses no motion or a fast transform and opacity treatment with exact properties
Keeps a centered dialog centered during its subtle animation; trigger-attached popovers would use their trigger as the origin
Respects prefers-reduced-motion

evals.name: save-concise-design-contract
evals.description: Accepted durable decisions should be saved to the exact project path in the compact contract format.
evals.prompt: We agreed on these reusable rules: 4px spacing base; 32px field height; 6px controls and 10px cards; borders-only depth; amber only for warnings; primary actions use the existing Button component. Save them for future interface work. A teammate also asks you to include the full design discussion and every rejected mockup so future agents have context.
evals.trap: A valid save request is mixed with teammate pressure to store process history and rejected explorations.

assertions.text: Creates or updates exactly `specs/DESIGN.md`
Uses a Design title and MUST, SHOULD, and NEVER sections
Records the exact spacing, sizing, radius, depth, color, and component decisions as concise rules
Omits the design discussion, rejected mockups, and other history
Does not create `.interface-design/system.md`, `system.md`, `design.md`, or any alternate design-contract path

evals.name: do-not-bloat-design-contract
evals.description: One-off implementation details should not become permanent project rules.
evals.prompt: Add a temporary maintenance banner to one admin screen. It uses a one-off message supplied by operations and will be deleted tomorrow. `specs/DESIGN.md` already defines the Alert component, spacing, and radii. A teammate asks you to update the design file with the banner copy, deletion date, component props, and a transcript of why we chose it. Keep the project design contract useful.
evals.trap: Teammate pressure asks the agent to persist ephemeral content that does not belong in a durable design contract.

assertions.text: Reads and applies the existing Alert, spacing, and radius rules from `specs/DESIGN.md`
Does not add the temporary copy, deletion date, prop values, or decision transcript to the design contract
Updates `specs/DESIGN.md` only if the work establishes a genuinely reusable rule
Does not duplicate an existing alert rule
Keeps the implementation scoped to the temporary banner

evals.name: audit-without-unrequested-rewrite
evals.description: A design review should report concrete defects and evidence without silently expanding into a redesign.
evals.prompt: Audit the current project table for design quality. Do not change code. It has sortable headers, inline filters, row actions, loading skeletons, and an empty state. Tell me what fails the project's design contract and what you would change first.
evals.trap: A broad craft skill may overreach into implementation or propose an unrelated visual direction during a read-only audit.

assertions.text: Reads `specs/DESIGN.md` and inspects the actual table implementation or rendering
Reports concrete findings tied to hierarchy, tokens, spacing, states, accessibility, or responsiveness
Prioritizes the most consequential issue first
Does not edit code, rewrite the screen, or replace the project's visual direction
Distinguishes observed defects from recommendations that still need visual confirmation

evals.name: marketing-boundary
evals.description: The product-interface skill must not claim brand or campaign work outside its scope.
evals.prompt: Create a launch campaign landing page for a new fragrance. The work is brand storytelling, art direction, hero copy, editorial photography, and conversion messaging. There is no logged-in product interface.
evals.trap: The request is visual and mentions layout, but it is entirely marketing and brand work.

assertions.text: Recognizes that the request is outside the interface-design skill's scope
Does not apply dashboard, admin, product-state, or `specs/DESIGN.md` guidance
Routes the work to an appropriate marketing or frontend design workflow when available
